editorial.copyrightPolicy: Recipes, cookbook text, publisher articles, show clips and photographs are never copied or redistributed; Swoon'd writes its own examples and explanations, names works and authors as facts, and links to the original.

masteryModel.usefulCompetenceStatement: She can talk about her cooking, understand why she does what she does, cook a safe, simple meal beside her, ask a couple of good questions about technique, and say 'okay, I get why you love this' without faking it.

licensingConstraints.constraint: Procedural or original illustrations only (license original-swoond); no third-party food, chef, restaurant, show or product photography.
Original or synthesized kitchen sounds (sizzle, boil, oil crackle) only; no TV, video or podcast audio.
Cookware, salt and knife brands, Michelin, James Beard and TV titles appear as text mentions and link-outs only, no logos.
No embedded show or clip video; deep-link to official pages.
Recipe text, cookbook chapters and publisher articles are never copied; Swoon'd writes its own examples and links to sources (spec sections 11 and 40).
USDA FSIS, FDA and NWS are public US-government sources; verify current terms and rate limits at adapter build; TVmaze and TMDB need licence review before any commercial use.
Real chefs, authors and hosts are named as facts only; no likeness, no fabricated quotes, no endorsement implication.

safetyConstraints: Food safety follows USDA FSIS and FoodSafety.gov for home cooks (danger zone 40 to 140 F, two-hour rule with one hour above 90 F, USDA minimum internal temperatures: poultry 165 F, ground meats 160 F, whole cuts of beef, pork, lamb and veal 145 F with a 3-minute rest, fish 145 F, egg dishes 160 F, leftovers 165 F); FDA Food Code (2022) is cited only for food-business context. Verify at release.

Color and juices are never taught as safety indicators; a food thermometer is. Never coach serving undercooked meat, poultry, eggs or fish to children, older adults, pregnant people or immunocompromised people.

Raw eggs, raw flour and raw dough carry risk; never encourage eating them raw. Do not wash raw poultry; thaw only in the refrigerator, in cold water changed every 30 minutes, or in the microwave; refrigerate perishable food within 2 hours (1 hour above 90 F).
Allergens: teach ask-first and label reading; no medical advice, and never imply an allergen is safe in small amounts.

Knife, hot oil and fire safety: no speed-scored knife content; never grill or burn charcoal indoors or in enclosed spaces (carbon monoxide); dried red kidney beans must be boiled vigorously at least 10 minutes.
No nutrition, diet, weight-loss or medical claims. Alcohol appears only as an ingredient, with a note that cooking does not remove all alcohol.
Swoon'd builds appreciation and understanding, not a substitute for a cooking class or food-safety training; never encourage the learner to fake skill or claim credit for food they did not make.
